Eschatology
(‘System of doctrines concerning death and after-life’)
------------------------------------------
The Hindu scriptures do not consider death as the final end of life and hence all the labours of a life properly lived, do not become null and void. They teach that there is life after the death of this physical body.
Hindu एस्छतोलोग्य् has four aspects. The first gives a prognostication of the approach of death. The second gives the rites to be performed by the dying person and/or his near relatives. The third deals with the obsequies to be undertaken just after death and later, over a period of time, up to one year. The fourth gives an account of what happens to the जीव (soul) after death.
Some of the signs that indicate the approach of death as described in the Śāntiparva of the Mahābhārata as also in the पुराणस् like the Vāyupurāṇa, Mārkaṇḍeyapurāṇa and Liṅgapurāṇa are as follows: not being able to see the star Arundhati or the pole-star or the full-मोओन्; not seeing one’s own reflection in the eyeball of another; seeing the orb of the मोओन् with a hole in it; smelling hot obnoxious odour of a corpse even though fragrant substances are brought near; loss of bodily heat; sudden oozing of moisture from the left eye; not hearing the humming sound in the ear, when the ears are closed with the fingers; not seeing the light when the eyes are closed and pressed by the fingers; dreaming of an ass or a त्रिशूल (trident) and so on.
As regards the second and third aspects, see ANTYEṢṬI and ŚRĀDDHA for details.
Now, coming to the fourth aspect, it is clearly guided by the theory of कर्म and rebirth.
In the उपनिषद्स्, three destinies are indicated for a dead person: to be reborn again and again which entails a lot of suffering; to go to पितृलोक by the dhūmādimārga or पितृयान; to go to ब्रह्मलोक by the arcirādimārga or देवयान, from which there is no return.
However, from the पितृलोक, which is like स्वर्ग or हेअवेन्, there is return to this world, after exhausting the fruits of all merit.
Those who have committed heinous crimes, called ‘mahāpātakas’ (like the murder of a ब्राह्मण or incest) go to abominable hells like अन्धतामिस्र, रौरव or kumbhīpāka. The पुराणस् enumerate as many as 32 such hells! They are probably different sections in the torture chambers of यम, the lord of death and the netherworld.
Those who have led a good life and have performed meritorious deeds as prescribed in the holy books, go to higher worlds such as स्वर्ग, महर्लोक, जनलोक and तपोलोक to enjoy themselves.
In both these cases, the souls return to this world the भूलोक, to continue the journey towards perfection.
